content: Indication-specific dosing for Acai palm (Euterpe oleracea), commonly known as Acai berry, includes the following details: 1. Typical Dosage: There is no standard dosage for Acai berry as it is often consumed as a food product. 2. Therapeutic Dosage for Anthocyanin/Flavonoid Content: 200–1500 mg per day is recommended for therapeutic purposes. 3. Adverse Effects: Commonly reported side effects include diarrhea, skin ulcers, and fever. 4. Acai Berry Juice: If well-tolerated, it can be consumed as needed. 5. Acai Berry Extract: A dosage of 500 mg per day is suggested. Adaptogenic Properties: Acai berry is considered an adaptogen, meaning it may help the body adapt to internal and external stressors, combat fatigue, and enhance stamina. Traditional Uses: Anti-aging benefits. Support for cardiovascular health, bone and joint health, and prostate/urinary tract health. Management of hypercholesterolemia. Detoxification and cleansing. Reduction of inflammation. Antioxidant Properties: Acai berry is a potent antioxidant with a high ORAC (Oxygen Radical Absorbance Capacity) value, which helps protect the body against free radical damage, infections, and diseases. Cardiovascular Benefits: Helps maintain healthy HDL cholesterol levels. Improves blood circulation. Reduces the risk of atherosclerosis, stroke, and heart attack. Exhibits COX-1 and COX-2 inhibitory activity, which may contribute to its anti-inflammatory effects. May act as a vasodilator, potentially benefiting individuals with cardiovascular diseases. Potential Use in Autoimmune Conditions: There is a possibility that Acai berry may provide benefits for conditions such as lupus, though further research is needed. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category: Not applicable (N/A). Lactation: Not applicable (N/A). Generally considered acceptable for use. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
